MIL methods cast medical images as bags of instances (e.g. patches in whole slide Probabilistic machine learning images, or slices in CT scans), and only bag labels are required for training. Deep MIL approaches have obtained Bayesian methods promising results by aggregating instance-level representations via an attention mechanism to compute the bag- Whole slide images level prediction. These methods typically capture both local interactions among adjacent instances and global, CT scans long-range dependencies through various mechanisms. However, they treat attention values deterministically, potentially overlooking uncertainty in the contribution of individual instances. In this work we propose a novel probabilistic framework that estimates a probability distribution over the attention values, and accounts for both global and local interactions. In a comprehensive evaluation involving eleven state-of-the-art baselines and three medical datasets, we show that our approach achieves top predictive performance in different metrics. JSON: Name: probsa_mil Title: Probabilistic smooth attention with Laplacian prior for deep multiple-instance learning in medical imaging Short Hypothesis: Modeling attention as a multivariate Gaussian variational distribution with a Laplacian (Dirichlet-energy) prior and combining local graph-based smoothing with a transformer encoder for global interactions will increase bag-level AUROC on medical MIL tasks and produce attention variance values that are positively correlated with instance-level prediction errors. Related Work: Existing deep multiple-instance learning (MIL) approaches follow two main families: attention-pooling methods that compute deterministic instance importance and graph- or transformer-based methods that capture local or global interactions respectively. Attention-based MIL produces interpretable instance scores but neglects inter-instance dependencies and provides no principled uncertainty quantification. Graph-based MIL introduces local smoothing via neighborhood relations but omits long-range dependencies; transformer-based MIL captures global pairwise dependencies through self-attention but treats attention values deterministically and may be sensitive to noisy instances. Recent deterministic smooth-attention methods add Laplacian regularization to enforce spatial coherence in attention but do not model uncertainty and typically lack global context. Limitations across these approaches include (1) absence of attention uncertainty estimates, (2) incomplete integration of both local and global interactions in a unified probabilistic framework, and (3) dependence on deterministic attention values that can produce false positive instance attributions without a measure of confidence. Abstract: We propose a probabilistic extension of smooth attention for deep multiple-instance learning in medical imaging that models instance attention as a multivariate Gaussian variational posterior and enforces local coherence with a Laplacian (Dirichlet-energy) prior while optionally incorporating global interactions via a transformer encoder. The method trains by maximizing a variational evidence lower bound where the KL term implements attention smoothness over a bag-level adjacency graph and the likelihood uses attention-weighted bag embedding. Main contributions are: (1) a unified probabilistic MIL architecture that jointly captures local and global instance interactions, (2) a tractable Gaussian variational attention that yields both mean attention for localization and per-instance uncertainty (variance) for reliability assessment, and (3) empirical evaluation on medical MIL benchmarks showing improved bag-level discrimination and interpretable uncertainty maps. Expected outcomes are higher bag-level AUROC compared to deterministic baselines and a measurable positive association between attention variance and incorrect instance-level attributions. Experiments: Datasets: RSNA intracranial hemorrhage CT dataset (n=1150 scans, 24–57 slices per scan), PANDA prostate whole-slide image dataset (10,616 WSIs at 10x), CAMELYON16 breast metastasis WSIs (400 WSIs at 20x). Extract instance features with a fixed pretrained backbone: ResNet50 ImageNet for RSNA, ResNet50 pretrained with pathology self-supervised method (Barlow Twins) for PANDA and CAMELYON16; output feature dim = 2048 then project to D=512 via a shared FC layer. Models and baselines: proposed ProbSA variants (ABMIL+ProbSA and T-ABMIL+ProbSA) with two posterior options (Σ=Diag Gaussian and Σ=0 Dirac); baselines: ABMIL, CLAM, DSMIL, PatchGCN, DTFD-MIL, TransMIL, SETMIL, GTP, IIBMIL, CAMIL, VMIL. Training protocol: 5-fold train/validation splits, 5 independent seeds, 100 epochs, Adam optimizer, base lr=1e-4, LinearLR warmup with start_factor=0.1 for 10 iters, batch size 32 for RSNA/PANDA, 4 (non-transformer) or 1 (transformer) for CAMELYON16; adjacency matrices constructed from feature-space inverse-distance and kept static. Hyperparameters and ablations: evaluate λ ∈ {0,0.1,0.5,1.0,cyclical} (cyclical schedule with M=5 cycles), compare Σ choices (Diag vs 0), compare bag transform H ∈ {per-instance MLP (ABMIL), TransformerEnc}, compare with and without Laplacian prior (adjacency off). Evaluation metrics and analyses: bag-level AUROC, F1, average rank across datasets; instance-level localization metrics where instance labels exist: patch-level AUROC/AUPR, IoU between thresholded attention and ground truth; calibration and uncertainty analyses: expected calibration error (ECE) on bag predictions, Pearson/Spearman correlation between per-instance attention variance and instance-level label errors, ROC of using variance as a flag for unreliable instance attributions; compute-time profiling: average time per training step and peak GPU memory. Ablation studies: (1) posterior type effect: Σ=Diag vs Σ=0 under both ABMIL and Transformer H, (2) λ schedule effect: compare fixed values vs cyclical, (3) adjacency effect: Laplacian prior on vs off, (4) uncertainty utility: measuring correlation between variance and localization error and effect on downstream precision when masking high-variance instances. Statistical reporting: report mean ± std across 5 runs and two-sided paired tests for AUROC differences (p<0.05). Hardware: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090. Risk Factors and Limitations: KL-collapse or posterior collapse when optimizing the variational posterior, reducing the model to a deterministic attention solution; sensitivity to the choice and scale of the Laplacian prior hyperparameter λ and to the adjacency construction, causing under- or over-smoothing across true class boundaries; high GPU memory and compute requirements for transformer-based global interaction on very large bags (huge WSIs), forcing aggressive batching or pre-extracted features; dependence on quality and domain-match of pretrained feature extractor—poor features degrade both bag-level performance and adjacency reliability; class imbalance in datasets can bias AUROC/F1 and localization evaluations and inflate average-rank comparisons; attention variance may be miscalibrated and not universally indicative of instance error across modalities; static adjacency ignores dynamic context and may not capture learned long-range structure; limited generalization to modalities with different spatial statistics or tasks where instance coherence assumptions do not hold.
